name: CA-51
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sara Jacobs with strong fundraising advantage
No general-election polls; challenger Ricardo Cabrera has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Jacobs near-certain to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Jacobs: a 10-point Democratic lean, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge against a little-known challenger with no visible resources. Markets price her at roughly 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the race unexpectedly competitive, or major outside spending for Cabrera, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sara Jacobs, the Democratic incumbent, is favored to win a second full term in this San Diego-area district, which leans Democratic by about 10 points. She advanced to the general election and has raised roughly $1.6 million, while Republican Ricardo Cabrera has no reported fundraising and no outside support on either side.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, Jacobs's financial advantage, and prediction markets, which price her chances at about 96%. The expected margin is roughly 21 points, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polling.
